newsitem.title: UK: Bass shares UK government alcohol concerns.
newsitem.headline: Bass shares UK government alcohol concerns.

text.p: Brewer to leisure group Bass Plc, which makes Britain's top-selling alcoholic soda Hoopers Hooch, said it shared government concerns over alcohol abuse.
Earlier, British Home Secretary Jack Straw said he had asked for an urgent inquiry, headed by George Howarth, into the consumption of alcoholic lemonades and sodas known as alcopops.
Bass shares fell 14p on the news to 816p.
"Bass shares the minister's concerns and welcomes the oppurtunity to meet with George Howarth to discuss the issue further," said Stuart Cain, press officer at Bass Brewers.

"Alcopops abuse is a real concern. We all know the links between alcohol abuse and crime," said Straw. "Everything must be done to stop young people falling into a downward spiral of offending," he added.

The decision comes a day after alcopop makers were condemned as "grossly irresponsible" by a judge after he heard how a 14-year-old boy got drunk on alcoholic lemonade and cider, and then burned down a school.
